title: Cashew Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Cashew Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Cashew nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium in kasoy, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Cashew nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your kasoy (cashew) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, zinc and boron. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Phosphorus deficiency on a leaf, shown on another crop as a stand in for cashew

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But zinc and boron stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which cashew nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a cashew nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest cashew nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in cashew

Older leaves turn pale green from the tip, then yellow and droop. The tree grows slowly, with smaller leaves and smaller fruits and nuts that mature early. In bad cases the young leaves pale too. You see it most at this stage: young trees in the first five years, and bearing trees that are never fertilized.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in kasoy
Most Philippine cashew trees get no fertilizer at all, as a review of cashew production in the Philippines notes. A study of cashew soils in coastal India found nitrogen only low to medium.
How to tell it apart

Tea mosquito bug damage also makes trees look poor. But it leaves dark dead lesions on young shoots and flower stalks, and the shoots and flower clusters dry up. To be sure, soil test, and a leaf test: a Brazilian study on dwarf cashew recommends the fifth or sixth mature leaf, counted from the flower cluster down the branch, taken at the start of flowering. New flushes that come out greener after urea confirm it.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

Apply Urea 46 0 0 or Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 in a ring under the canopy and water it in, following the soil test. Kerala Agricultural University gives a full yearly dose of 750 grams of nitrogen per tree from the fifth year, with one fifth of that in the first year and one fifth more each year after. For a quick lift it gives a foliar spray of Urea at 10 grams per liter every 15 days.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, fertilize young trees every year as they grow, split the dose over the rainy season, and mulch the basin.
Phosphorus deficiency in cashew

Young mature leaves first turn darker green, then take on a dull red, green or purple tint. The tree stays small with less leaf area, leaves fall early, and some branches die back with dead leaf tips. You see it most at this stage: young trees after planting and trees on poor acid soils.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in kasoy
Acid, weathered upland soils that lock up phosphorus and soils low in organic matter. A study of cashew soils in coastal Karnataka, India found phosphorus highly deficient in every soil profile.
How to tell it apart

Potassium deficiency also brings purple spots, but on the underside of leaves, together with yellow, browning leaf edges. Tea mosquito bug causes shoot dieback too, but with dark lesions on the shoots. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus and pH, and a leaf test of mature leaves taken at the start of flowering.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Kerala Agricultural University advises Superphosphate for a quick fix and rock phosphate or bone meal for the long term, applied after a soil test. Its full yearly dose for trees from the fifth year is 325 grams of P2O5 per tree. Phosphorus is taken up best near pH 6.5 to 7.5, so lime very acid soils.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, put phosphorus in the planting hole, add organic manure each year, and lime acid soils.
Potassium deficiency in cashew

The edges of older leaves turn pale yellow, then brown and die, and the damage moves up to younger leaves. In bad cases the whole leaf browns. Purple spots can show on the underside of leaves. Trees grow poorly and give smaller, lighter nuts. You see it most at this stage: bearing trees, most of all during nut filling.
Why potassium deficiency happens in kasoy
Sandy and leached soils, acid soils, and years of harvest with no potash returned. Potash is readily available above about pH 6.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium deficiency also starts on old leaves, but it yellows between the veins rather than scorching the edge. Drought can also brown leaf edges, but over the whole tree at once. To be sure, soil test for potash and pH, and a leaf test of mature leaves at the start of flowering.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Kerala Agricultural University advises Muriate of potash 0 0 60 in split doses following the soil test. Lime or dolomite to keep pH up. Its full yearly dose for trees from the fifth year is 750 grams of K2O per tree. For a quick fix spray Sulfate of potash at 10 grams per liter in the morning. TNAU gives a 1 percent potassium chloride spray.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, give potash every year with nitrogen, add organic matter, and keep the soil pH near 6.
Zinc deficiency in cashew

The youngest leaves come out small and long, green to pale green with the veins staying green. Sometimes show small dead spots. Internodes stay short and the tree makes few side branches. You see it most at this stage: new flushes, mostly before flowering.
Why zinc deficiency happens in kasoy
Soils naturally low in zinc, heavy phosphate, and pH outside 5 to 7.5. The coastal Karnataka cashew soil study found zinc highly deficient in every soil profile.
How to tell it apart

Manganese deficiency also bunches the leaves into a rosette. But the leaves are pale green to greenish yellow and the tree makes more side branches, not fewer. To be sure, soil test for zinc and pH, and a leaf test of mature leaves at the start of flowering. Spray a few trees and watch the next flush.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

In bad cases Kerala Agricultural University gives a morning spray of Zinc sulfate at 2 grams per liter mixed with 2.5 grams per liter of lime (calcium carbonate). TNAU gives Zinc sulfate at 0.5 percent (5 grams per liter). Do not apply zinc and phosphate fertilizer at the same time.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester, Inc. (22 percent zinc), **Great Planters Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (21 percent zinc), **Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** by Petbowe Trading Corporation (33 percent zinc) and **YaraVita ZINTRAC 700** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (40 percent zinc). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, avoid heavy phosphate and overliming, and spray zinc before flowering where tests run low.
Boron deficiency in cashew

It hits the growing points. Buds and young leaves die, and root tips stop growing, lose color and die. Flowers drop, the fruits split, and nuts stay small and poorly filled. You see it most at this stage: flushing and flowering, and during nut setting.
Why boron deficiency happens in kasoy
No cashew particular causes were found in the sources. In other tree crops such as coffee, it is linked to soils low in boron, heavy liming, heavy potash and long droughts.
How to tell it apart

Tea mosquito bug also dries flower clusters and kills young shoots, but it leaves dark lesions where it fed. Calcium deficiency also kills growing points, but the young leaves ripple, turn brittle and cup with scorched edges. To be sure, soil test for boron, and a leaf test of mature leaves at the start of flowering.
What to apply for boron deficiency

After a soil test, Kerala Agricultural University gives Borax to the soil at 50 grams per tree, or a foliar spray of Borax at 1 gram per liter. Do not mix borax with calcium or ammonium fertilizers. Too much boron is toxic, so do not repeat high doses without a test.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add organic matter, mulch the basin in the dry season.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any cashew nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your kasoy needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Cashew nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my kasoy leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: old leaves pale from the tip, then yellow and droopy. Small leaves, small nuts. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at zinc deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in cashew?
items.a: Apply Urea 46 0 0 or Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 in a ring under the canopy and water it in, following the soil test. Kerala Agricultural University gives a full yearly dose of 750 grams of nitrogen per tree from the fifth year, with one fifth of that in the first year and one fifth more each year after.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in cashew?
items.a: Kerala Agricultural University advises Superphosphate for a quick fix and rock phosphate or bone meal for the long term, applied after a soil test. Its full yearly dose for trees from the fifth year is 325 grams of P2O5 per tree.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in cashew?
items.a: Kerala Agricultural University advises Muriate of potash 0 0 60 in split doses following the soil test. Lime or dolomite to keep pH up.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my kasoy lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the cashew nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
